problem_text:
We have an undirected graph with 3 vertices (numbered 0..2) and 3 edges:
  edges = (0,1), (0,2), (1,2)

Each vertex must receive one of 3 colors (0, 1, 2).
Color code per vertex v (2 qubits): low bit b0 = problem_qubits[2v], high bit b1 = problem_qubits[2v+1]; code value c = b0 + 2*b1.
Decoding is SURJECTIVE: c=0 (binary 00) -> color 0, c=1 (01) -> color 1, c=2 (10) -> color 2, and c=3 (binary 11) ALSO decodes to color 0.
All 2-bit codes are legal; there is no invalid code.
Worked example with the 11 code: if vertex 0 has code 11 and vertex 1 has code 00, both decode to color 0, so an edge (0,1) would be monochromatic and the constraint 'colors differ' is VIOLATED.

The classical predicate is f(x) = 1 if and only if, after decoding every vertex's 2-bit code to its color, every edge connects two vertices of DIFFERENT colors.
